title: Reporting offers, suggestions, orders, intentions, etc.
subtitle: She encouraged Fran to take the job.
summary: Report offers, orders, promises and suggestions with the pattern each verb allows: a to-infinitive, an object + to-infinitive, a that-clause or an -ing clause.

lesson.heading: to-infinitive with or without an object

left.label: Verb + to-infinitive
left.text: No object comes between the verb and the to-infinitive. Also: agree, demand, guarantee, offer, promise, swear, threaten, volunteer.
examples: 'The theatre will be built next to the town hall.' -> They **propose to build** the theatre next to the town hall.
not ~~They propose them to build the theatre~~
He **agreed to collect** Declan from school.

right.label: Verb + object + to-infinitive
right.text: The object is the person the offer or order is made to - the one who performs the reported action. Also: advise, ask, call on, command, instruct, invite, order, persuade, recommend, remind, request, urge, warn, tell.
examples: 'You should take the job, Fran.' -> She **encouraged Fran to take** the job.
He **called on the government to do** more to help the homeless.

lesson.note: Compare: We asked to leave our bags outside the exam room. (= we wanted this) and They asked us to leave our bags outside the exam room. (= they wanted this)

lesson.heading: that-clause instead of a to-infinitive
lesson.text: After some verbs a that-clause is an alternative. Also: agree, demand, expect, guarantee, hope, propose, request, vow. The that-clause is useful because the two subjects can be different people.

examples.text: He promised **to arrive** on time. = He promised **that he would arrive** on time.
He promised **that he wouldn't be** late.
examples.note: 'He' and 'he' may refer to different people

lesson.heading: that-clause only
lesson.text: After **insist**, **order**, **say** and **suggest** we use a that-clause and never a to-infinitive. Advise and order can take either an object + to-infinitive or a that-clause.

examples.text: There were cheers when he suggested **that we went** home early.
examples.wrong: he suggested to go home early

examples.note: or I advised her to accept.; but not ~~I advised to accept~~

examples.text: She said **that she expected** to see improvements within a year.

lesson.heading: to-infinitive only
lesson.text: After some verbs we use a to-infinitive but never a that-clause. Also: long, offer, refuse, volunteer, want.

examples.text: Carolyn **intends to return** to Dublin after a year in Canada.
examples.wrong: Carolyn intends that she should return

examples.text: He **hoped that** the Narian president would act now.
examples.wrong: He wanted that the Narian president would act

lesson.heading: Reporting a suggestion with an -ing clause
lesson.text: With **advise**, **propose**, **recommend** and **suggest** we can report a suggestion with an -ing clause instead of a that-clause. This works whether the suggestion is about the speaker or about somebody else.

examples.text: The lecturer recommended **reading** a number of books before the exam.
examples.note: or ... recommended that the students should read ...

examples.text: To avoid the road works, police have advised **leaving** the motorway at Junction 3.
The council proposed **reducing** bus and train fares.
examples.note: propose also allows a to-infinitive: proposed to reduce fares

lesson.text: *demand* and *insist* look similar but behave differently: *demanded that troops withdraw*, but ~~demanded troops to withdraw~~ - use *ordered* for that pattern.

exercises.prompt: Match each set of words with its report.

pairs.right: He asked me to lend him ten pounds.
He ordered us to be quiet.

pairs.left: 'I will fight the ban on smoking in public places.'
pairs.right: He vowed to fight the ban on smoking in public places.

pairs.left: 'If I were you, I'd read the exam questions very carefully.'
pairs.right: He advised us to read the exam questions very carefully.

pairs.left: 'Please stay for a few more days.'
pairs.right: He urged me to stay for a few more days.

exercises.prompt: 'Okay, I'll collect Declan from school.' -> He ___ to collect Declan from school.
exercises.explanation: agree takes a plain to-infinitive - no object comes in between.

exercises.prompt: 'The government should do more to help the homeless.' -> He ___ to do more to help the homeless.
exercises.explanation: call on needs an object before the to-infinitive: called on the government to do more.

exercises.prompt: 'I imagine I'll see Olivia at the party.' -> He ___ to see Olivia at the party.
exercises.explanation: Both verbs report an expectation and take a plain to-infinitive.

exercises.prompt: Which report of 'Why don't we go home early?' is correct?
options: He suggested that we went home early.
He suggested to go home early.
He suggested us to go home early.
exercises.explanation: suggest takes a that-clause (or an -ing clause), never a to-infinitive.

exercises.prompt: Ricardo said the play was very entertaining and he recommended ___ it.
exercises.explanation: advise, propose, recommend and suggest can report a suggestion with an -ing clause.

exercises.statement: In a major speech today, the Health Minister suggested to improve the country's health care.
exercises.explanation: ... the Health Minister promised to improve the country's health care. suggest cannot be followed by a to-infinitive.

exercises.statement: She guaranteed to reduce waiting times for operations.
exercises.explanation: Correct. guarantee takes a to-infinitive (and also allows a that-clause).

exercises.statement: The President of Guwandi has demanded Narian troops to withdraw from the border area.
exercises.explanation: ... has ordered Narian troops to withdraw from the border area. demand cannot take an object + to-infinitive.

exercises.statement: The UN Secretary General has offered that a peace conference should be held in New York.
exercises.explanation: ... has proposed that a peace conference should be held in New York. offer takes a to-infinitive, not a that-clause.

exercises.prompt: Which pattern does each reporting verb allow?
The invigilators wanted the bags left outside. Report what they said.
exercises.answer: They asked us to leave our bags outside the exam room
exercises.explanation: With an object, ask reports what somebody wanted us to do; without one it reports what we wanted.
